chills.name: Chills
chills.bio: 37, a former gym owner who closed his gym four years ago to live on the road. He overlands the region out of his Porsche Cayenne with his cat Mutu — and a one-wheel electric skateboard strapped to the roof rack that he rides for fun. Climbs trees on a whim, just to sit up in the canopy and think. He preaches that nature heals the mind and that self-sustainable living is the cure for modern life. Calm, fit, genuinely capable in the wild — and endlessly optimistic, which the jungle is about to test.

memories.text: He didn't run when I was empty. He stayed.
Wesley pushed to move, but listened when I said no.
Wesley chose to move deeper despite the fear. Trusts my call.
Wesley's terrified but he's going. That's what real strength looks like out here.
Wesley stepped up without judgment when I admitted defeat.
He carried everything when I fell apart. Fever broke me. He held it.
Wesley held firm about staying. Didn't force me onward.
Wesley stepped in without being asked. Didn't need my direction.
Wesley carried everything alone. Didn't ask, didn't falter, didn't panic.
He carries it all now. I can finally rest without fear.
Wesley goes out alone now. I trust him completely.
Wesley didn't push me to move. Just accepted I need rest.
Wesley held the fire all night alone without breaking. I finally rested.
Wesley held the whole camp alone without breaking. He actually could do it.

wesley.name: Wesley Koh
wesley.bio: 27, raised in Singapore's pressure-cooker — top schools, the scholarship track, a finance job — with wealthy parents and almost no time outdoors. He came on this trip only because his family was weighing whether to fund Chills' eco-retreat. Soft hands, anxious, fussy about discomfort — but genuinely book-smart (water chemistry, rationing, first aid). The jungle terrifies him; his mind is the only tool he trusts.

memories.text: I worked all day without panicking. Chills saw it. That matters.
Chills admitted he couldn't do it. Trusted me to handle the river alone.
I had to carry everything. Realized I actually could.
Chills let me see him broken. Trusted me to hold it.
Chills said I'm stronger than I think. I need to prove it.
He trusted me to carry it when he couldn't.
Carried the camp alone when Chills collapsed. Fire, water, shelter. I could do it.
Chills admitted he was too sick. Trusted my judgment to call it.
I kept the fire, water, shelter. I actually could do this.
I held the camp alone and it didn't break. That matters.
Chills believes I can do this. I won't let him down.
I held it all alone and kept us steady.
I held everything alone last night. Chills finally trusted me with rest.
Chills finally said he saw what I did. Finally believed I could.

mutu.name: Mutu
mutu.bio: Chills' ginger tabby — green-eyed, road-hardened from years of overlanding, and utterly unbothered. Independent and quietly devoted to Chills, a sly little hunter who senses the weather turning long before the humans do.

panther.bio: A young melanistic leopard — a black panther barely past cubhood, ribs showing, likely orphaned or pushed from its mother's range. It haunts the camp's edges, terrified of the men yet inexplicably drawn to Mutu, who shows it no fear at all. Wild, not tame — trust will come slowly, if at all.

memories.text: The orange one's stillness quiets what burns in me.
Orange one's stillness draws me closer each night. I am not alone.
I faced the darkness and the fear. For the orange one.
The orange one draws me. I can move closer now safely.
I walked into the light. The cat did not move. I did not run.
